messages:
elena: Heads-up: Launchpad onboarding hit a burst of 429s right after ephemeral key rotation this morning. Attaching logs + their init pattern.
elena: logs:
```
2026-03-24T11:02:33Z WARN preflight validate status=429 path=/v1/preflight/validate retry-after=1
2026-03-24T11:02:34Z ERROR request failed status=429 path=/v1/chat/completions client_id=launchpad-prod origin=eu-west-1
2026-03-24T11:02:34Z WARN concurrent token requests=64 origin=ec2-3-8-99-22.eu-west-1.compute.amazonaws.com
```
elena: Their onboarding harness spins up 64 parallel Go workers in CI that fetch ephemeral from our /tokens/ephemeral then immediately do chat.create. Theyre on go-sdk v0.4.0.
rafa: sys-bot posted an alert earlier :sys-bot:
sys-bot: [alert] rate_limit_spike account=launchpad region=eu-west window=00:00:12 peak_rps=210 baseline_rps=18 id=rl-20260324-11
rafa: sounds like a rotate stampede. Immediate suggestions: 1) ask them to switch to a server-side token broker or an in-process token cache in CI; 2) add a small concurrency cap (~8-10) and jittered exponential backoff in the init flow; 3) we can open a short priority window (60-120s) to drain inflight requests while they patch.
elena: customer init snippet they shared (Go):
```go
client := redwood.NewClient(os.Getenv("EPH_KEY"))
for i := 0; i < 64; i++ {
  go func() {
    _, err := client.Chat.Create(ctx, req)
    if err != nil { log.Println(err) }
  }()
}
```
elena: note: they fetch ephemeral directly from clients in CI; no broker.
sam: i'll take customer comms. elena, can you confirm if calls are hitting /preflight/validate or /tokens first?
elena: majority hit /tokens/ephemeral then preflight + chat.
sam: message i'll send: "we observed a short-lived fanout during your key rotation. Recommended immediate step: gate ephemeral exchange behind a single CI broker or add a 2s token cache + limit concurrent init to 8 with jittered backoff. We'll enable a 90s elevated priority window to let existing inflight requests drain." ok?
rafa: infra note: i'll enable short-term coalesce rule for account=launchpad when concurrent preflight >50 in 15s. That will dedupe identical ephemeral/token checks for 120s. Apply rule id rl-20260324-11:coalesce. Watch for small tail latency increase.
sam: suggested backoff snippet (sent to customer):
```go
sem := make(chan struct{}, 8) // cap concurrency
for attempt := 0; attempt < 5; attempt++ {
  sem <- struct{}{}
  _, err := client.Chat.Create(ctx, req)
  <-sem
  if err == nil { break }
  if is429(err) { time.Sleep(time.Duration((1<<attempt))*100*time.Millisecond + jitter()) }
}
```
elena: customer replied: "we can change CI harness but mobile team wants direct ephemeral fetch for quick local dev." they asked for a lightweight in-device cache pattern and a one-paragraph note for renewal docs.
sam: recommend a small token broker pattern: single ephemeral-exchange endpoint that caches identical requests for 1-2s and returns same ephemeral to clients if within window. Also recommend rotating keys in staged fashion (roll subsets of test runners) to avoid global fanout.
rafa: marking infra change rl-20260324-11:coalesce applied for account=launchpad window=120s. Also enabling a temporary soft quota bump for 90s to reduce failed inits while they deploy patch.
sam: quick follow-up: after they applied 8-concurrency cap + broker for CI, 429s dropped ~94% within 2 minutes. They're asking for a one-paragraph renewal blurb and a short "rotation checklist" to include in their contract appendix.
